title: OSHA general industry lockout/tagout practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry lockout/tagout practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.147. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Another standard in 29 CFR Part 1910 requires the use of lockout. Under 1910.147(a)(3)(ii), how does the lockout/tagout standard apply to that requirement?

options.A: It does not apply, because the other standard replaces it
options.B: Lockout is used and supplemented by the procedural and training requirements of 1910.147
options.C: It applies only if the other standard is more than ten years old
options.D: It applies only to the training records, not to the procedures

questions.explanation: The purpose paragraph states: "When other standards in this part require the use of lockout or tagout, they shall be used and supplemented by the procedural and training requirements of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A hot tap is to be made on a pressurized steam pipeline. Under 1910.147(a)(2)(iii)(B), what must the employer demonstrate for the hot tap to fall outside the lockout/tagout standard?

options.A: That the pipeline pressure has been lowered below 15 psig
options.B: That a warning tag has been hung on the nearest upstream valve
options.C: That the welder holds a current hot work permit and nothing more
options.D: That continuity of service is essential, shutdown of the system is impractical, and documented procedures and special equipment giving proven effective protection are used

questions.explanation: Hot tap operations on pressurized pipelines are excluded "provided that the employer demonstrates that" continuity of service is essential, shutdown of the system is impractical, and "documented procedures are followed, and special equipment is used which will provide proven effective protection for employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Servicing that takes place during normal production operations is covered by 1910.147 when which of these is true?

options.A: An employee is required to remove or bypass a guard or other safety device
options.B: The servicing is done by an outside contractor
options.C: The machine has run for more than eight hours that day
options.D: The operator asks for a lockout

questions.explanation: Servicing during normal production operations is covered only if "an employee is required to remove or bypass a guard or other safety device" or must place part of his or her body into the point of operation or an associated danger zone.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An energy isolating device has no hasp and no built-in locking mechanism. Under the 1910.147(b) definition, when is it still "capable of being locked out"?

options.A: When a tag can be tied to its handle
options.B: When it is painted a standard safety color
options.C: When lockout can be achieved without the need to dismantle, rebuild or replace the device or permanently alter its energy control capability
options.D: When it is located within sight of the machine it controls

questions.explanation: Under the definition, "Other energy isolating devices are capable of being locked out, if lockout can be achieved without the need to dismantle, rebuild, or replace the energy isolating device or permanently alter its energy control capability."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the definitions in 1910.147, when does an affected employee become an authorized employee?

options.A: After one year of operating the machine
options.B: When the employee's name appears on a tag hung by someone else
options.C: When that employee's duties include performing servicing or maintenance covered under the section
options.D: When a supervisor is watching the employee

questions.explanation: "An affected employee becomes an authorized employee when that employee's duties include performing servicing or maintenance covered under this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: If an energy isolating device is not capable of being locked out, what must the employer's energy control program use?

options.A: A tagout system
options.B: Only the machine's stop button
options.C: A verbal warning to coworkers
options.D: No energy control

questions.explanation: "If an energy isolating device is not capable of being locked out, the employer's energy control program under paragraph (c)(1) of this section shall utilize a tagout system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After January 2, 1990, when new machines are installed, how must their energy isolating devices be designed?

options.A: With push-button stops in place of disconnects
options.B: With a holder for warning tags only
options.C: With a selector switch for each operator
options.D: To accept a lockout device

questions.explanation: After January 2, 1990, whenever new machines or equipment are installed (or replacement or major repair, renovation or modification is performed), energy isolating devices "shall be designed to accept a lockout device."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When a tagout device is used on an energy isolating device that is capable of being locked out, where must the tag be attached?

options.A: On the operator's control panel
options.B: At the same location that the lockout device would have been attached
options.C: On the main entrance door to the work area
options.D: On the machine's power cord

questions.explanation: "the tagout device shall be attached at the same location that the lockout device would have been attached," and the employer must show the tagout program gives a level of safety equivalent to lockout.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these is one of the items 1910.147(c)(4)(ii) says the energy control procedures must include?

options.A: Specific requirements for testing a machine or equipment to verify the effectiveness of lockout devices, tagout devices and other energy control measures
options.B: The production quota for the machine
options.C: The purchase price of each lock
options.D: The manufacturer's warranty terms

questions.explanation: The listed items include "Specific requirements for testing a machine or equipment to determine and verify the effectiveness of lockout devices, tagout devices, and other energy control measures."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Tags will be used in an area where acid and alkali chemicals are handled and stored. Which requirement does 1910.147(c)(5)(ii)(A) set for them?

options.A: They must be replaced at the start of every shift
options.B: They shall not deteriorate when used in corrosive environments
options.C: They must be kept in a sealed cabinet next to the machine
options.D: They may be replaced by a verbal warning to the crew

questions.explanation: Under the "Durable" requirement, "Tags shall not deteriorate when used in corrosive environments such as areas where acid and alkali chemicals are handled and stored."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A maintenance department keeps a supply of padlocks issued as lockout devices. Under 1910.147(c)(5)(ii), may those padlocks also be used to secure a tool cabinet?

options.A: Yes, if the padlock is labeled with the cabinet number
options.B: Yes, between lockout jobs
options.C: Yes, if a supervisor approves it in writing
options.D: No; lockout devices shall not be used for other purposes

questions.explanation: Lockout devices and tagout devices "shall be the only devices(s) used for controlling energy; shall not be used for other purposes".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the "Identifiable" requirement, what must lockout and tagout devices indicate?

options.A: The date the device was purchased
options.B: The machine's serial number
options.C: The identity of the employee applying the device
options.D: The supervisor's phone number

questions.explanation: "Lockout devices and tagout devices shall indicate the identity of the employee applying the device(s)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where tagout is used for energy control, the periodic inspection under 1910.147(c)(6)(i)(D) must include a review between the inspector and whom?

options.A: The plant manager only
options.B: The OSHA area office
options.C: The person who wrote the procedure only
options.D: Each authorized and affected employee

questions.explanation: Where tagout is used, "the periodic inspection shall include a review, between the inspector and each authorized and affected employee, of that employee's responsibilities under the energy control procedure being inspected" and the elements in paragraph (c)(7)(ii).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to 1910.147(c)(6)(i)(B), what is the periodic inspection of an energy control procedure conducted to do?

options.A: Correct any deviations or inadequacies identified
options.B: Measure the machine's production output
options.C: Rank authorized employees for promotion
options.D: Set the department's energy cost budget

questions.explanation: The rule states: "The periodic inspection shall be conducted to correct any deviations or inadequacies identified."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What must the employer's certification of a periodic inspection identify?

options.A: The hours of machine downtime and the cost of repairs
options.B: The names of the machine's suppliers
options.C: The machine or equipment, the date of the inspection, the employees included and the person performing it
options.D: Only the year in which the inspection took place

questions.explanation: "The certification shall identify the machine or equipment on which the energy control procedure was being utilized, the date of the inspection, the employees included in the inspection, and the person performing the inspection."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.147(c)(7)(i)(B), each affected employee must be instructed in what?

options.A: How to apply his or her own lock to the machine being serviced
options.B: The purpose and use of the energy control procedure
options.C: Nothing; only authorized employees receive instruction
options.D: Only the location of the first-aid kit

questions.explanation: "Each affected employee shall be instructed in the purpose and use of the energy control procedure." Under 1910.147(c)(8), "Lockout or tagout shall be performed only by the authorized employees who are performing the servicing or maintenance."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A periodic inspection reveals that an employee's use of the energy control procedure deviates from it. What does 1910.147(c)(7)(iii)(B) require?

options.A: Nothing until the next annual inspection
options.B: Removal of the employee's lock from the group lockbox for one month
options.C: Additional retraining
options.D: A written report to the OSHA area office

questions.explanation: "Additional retraining shall also be conducted whenever a periodic inspection under paragraph (c)(6) of this section reveals, or whenever the employer has reason to believe, that there are deviations from or inadequacies in the employee's knowledge or use of the energy control procedures."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A tag cannot be affixed directly to an energy isolating device. Where does 1910.147(d)(4)(iii)(B) require the tag to be located?

options.A: As close as safely possible to the device, in a position that will be immediately obvious to anyone attempting to operate it
options.B: On the door of the maintenance shop
options.C: In the lockout logbook kept by the supervisor
options.D: On the authorized employee's hard hat

questions.explanation: "Where a tag cannot be affixed directly to the energy isolating device, the tag shall be located as close as safely possible to the device, in a position that will be immediately obvious to anyone attempting to operate the device."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The authorized employee who applied a lock has gone home, and the lock is to be removed under the employer's direction. Which element must the employer's specific removal procedure include?

options.A: Cutting the lock only in the presence of an OSHA inspector
options.B: Verification by the employer that the authorized employee who applied the device is not at the facility
options.C: Waiting 24 hours after the end of the employee's shift
options.D: Having the next shift's machine operator sign the tag

questions.explanation: The specific procedure must include at least "Verfication by the employer that the authorized employee who applied the device is not at the facility" (spelling as in the eCFR text), reasonable efforts to contact that employee, and making sure the employee knows before resuming work.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.147, The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout) (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In group lockout or tagout, what must each authorized employee do when he or she begins work?

options.A: Sign a sheet kept by the crew leader instead of using a device
options.B: Hand his or her lock to the crew leader to apply
options.C: Rely on the operations lock alone
options.D: Affix a personal lockout or tagout device to the group lockout device, group lockbox or comparable mechanism

questions.explanation: "Each authorized employee shall affix a personal lockout or tagout device to the group lockout device, group lockbox, or comparable mechanism when he or she begins work," and remove it when he or she stops working on the machine.
